newsitem.title: KENYA: Bourses in Uganda, Tanzania seen boosting Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Bourses in Uganda, Tanzania seen boosting Kenya.

text.p: The opening of stock markets in Uganda and Tanzania will help lift the Nairobi Stock Exchange and improve the regional investment climate, Barclays Bank of Kenya Ltd managing director Peter Geer said.

"The Nairobi bourse will gain...because there will be a general growth in interest in the whole East African region on the part of foreign investors. It will create a bigger market, I could see growth of East African funds," Geer told Reuters.
Stock exchanges in Tanzania and Uganda are to be launched later this year.

"Investment advisers and managers in Europe or in America are setting aside a certain percentage of their investment to invest within the region. There will be a spin-off advantage to Nairobi in this," Geer said in an interview on Wednesday.

"It's quite possible some of those shares having been quoted on the Kampala Exchange could also be quoted in Nairobi. For nationalistic reasons they (Uganda and Tanzania) will be determined to have their own exchanges rather than rely on Nairobi," Geer added.
He said companies listed on the Nairobi Stock Exchange should provide more information about their financial status and strategies.
"More information from companies would be beneficial. Many of them just keep quiet for a whole year, just issue the minimal annual report and do not (do) any more," Geer said.
Established in 1954, the Nairobi bourse had a market capitalisation of 105 billion shillings ($1.8 billion at 1995 rates) at end-December 1995. It has 59 listed companies.
Barclays, a blue-chip company, is one of Kenya's four top retail banks. The others are Standard Chartered Bank, Kenya Commercial Bank and National Bank of Kenya.
